name: Syrus AI
author: jobbe99

sections.description:
Syrus AI brings a set of AI assisted tools into the WordPress admin:

  • AI Translate — translate a post of your own site into another language from the editor sidebar. The translation becomes a draft linked to the original, with its categories, tags and featured image; nothing is published and the original is untouched.
  • Social sharing — when a post is published, generate a caption for it and share it on the connected Facebook, Instagram, X/Twitter and LinkedIn accounts. Which posts get shared is decided by category and tag.
  • Contact forms — build a form, place it with the [syrus_contact_form] shortcode, protect it with Cloudflare Turnstile and have submissions emailed to the address you choose.
  • AI featured image — generate the featured image of a post from its title and content.

Under Tools there is a second set, for running the site rather than writing it. None of it involves AI, and each one is off until you configure it:

  • Code injection — add markup to the head, to the footer, around the body of an article and between its paragraphs, without editing the theme. A single post can opt out of any of it.
  • Editorial checks — thirteen rules an article has to satisfy before it can go public, each one a switch. A post that breaks one goes back to Pending with the problems listed in the Publish box.
  • Content filters — strip the markup Word and Google Docs leave behind, and rewrite http:// links as https://.
  • robots.txt and ads.txt — serve both files from the database instead of uploading them.
  • WhatsApp chat — a bubble in the corner of the site that opens a conversation on WhatsApp. It works with any theme.
  • Maintenance — close the comments on older posts, drop their revisions, clear the spam and empty the moderation queue, and restrict who may upload files.

Credits / Resources

This plugin bundles the following third-party assets:

  • Select2 4.0.13 — MIT — https://select2.org/
  • SweetAlert2 11.7.18 — MIT — https://sweetalert2.github.io/

External Services Info & Usage

This plugin relies on a proprietary server that brokers the calls to the third-party services, so the plugin itself holds no credentials for them beyond the API keys you enter. Communication uses REST over HTTPS and JSON, authenticated with a token unique to each installation. The only data sent for authentication is the domain the plugin is installed on.

  1. https://developers.syrus.it/api/wp/v1/install and /uninstall
    Registers and deregisters the installation, returning the token that authenticates every later call. Sent on activation and on deletion.
    Terms of Use: https://syrusindustry.com/wordpress/plugin/syrus-ai/terms-of-use

  2. https://developers.syrus.it/api/wp/v1/{facebook,instagram,twitter,linkedin}/share and /revoke, and /auth_url
    Publishes a post on a connected account, connects an account and revokes its token. Sent when you publish a post with sharing enabled, or act on the Social Network screen.
    Terms of Use: https://syrusindustry.com/wordpress/plugin/syrus-ai/terms-of-use

  3. https://developers.syrus.it/api/wp/v1/import/configuration
    Imports the plugin configuration from another installation, when you paste a configuration token.
    Terms of Use: https://syrusindustry.com/wordpress/plugin/syrus-ai/terms-of-use

The AI provider you connect under Settings > Connectors is called directly by WordPress’s own AI Client, with the key WordPress holds: which service that is, and its terms, depend on the provider plugin you installed.

  1. https://api-free.deepl.com/v2/translate
    Translates text, using the DeepL key you enter. Sent when you translate an article.
    Terms of Use: https://www.deepl.com/pro-license
    Privacy Policy: https://www.deepl.com/privacy

  2. https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify
    Verifies the captcha of a contact form submission, when Turnstile protection is enabled for that form.
    Terms of Use: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/
    Privacy Policy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/

Privacy

Contact form submissions are emailed to the address configured for the form and are not stored in the database. The values shown on the thank-you page are held in a transient for five minutes and then discarded.

The plugin logs its own activity in two tables: a readable log of what it did, and a technical log of the requests to the AI services, which contains the prompts and the answers. The credentials are masked. If the content you translate or generate carries personal data, that data is in the technical log too, so consider it when setting your retention policy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the syrus-ai folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin from the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  2. Activate it from the Plugins screen.
  3. Connect an AI provider under Settings → Connectors: that is where WordPress keeps the keys, and this plugin reads them from there. With the Syrus theme active, the plugin appears under the theme menu as AI Support.

Entering the API keys requires administrator permissions. The rest of the plugin is available to editors.
sections.faq:
Which API keys do I need?

None are stored by this plugin. Text and image generation go through the AI provider you connect under Settings → Connectors, which is WordPress’s own screen: install one of the provider plugins listed there, paste the key once, and every plugin on the site can use it. DeepL registers itself in the same screen and is optional — when it is configured it does the translating, otherwise the AI provider does. Social sharing goes through the Syrus backend and needs no key of its own.

Does deactivating the plugin delete my data?

No. Up to version 0.4.5 it did: deactivation dropped all four tables. Since 0.5.0 the data is removed only when the plugin is deleted.

Enable the schedule in Settings, pick the hour, then have an external scheduler call the URL shown under Scheduler URL on that same screen. The URL carries a secret key that authenticates the call, so keep it private.

Why is my contact form rejecting submissions?

Check the language filter under Settings. It discards submissions from browsers that do not declare it-IT. It is off by default, and was unconditional before 0.5.0.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • The contact form on the front end is styled by the plugin at last. It was written in Bootstrap classes the plugin never loaded there, so it looked right only on a theme that happened to bring Bootstrap with it and came out as a bare stack of inputs everywhere else. It now carries a small stylesheet of its own, loaded only on a page that shows the form, scoped so it reaches nothing else, and built on custom properties a theme can redefine.
  • The summary shown on the thank-you page was in the same state, and it gave up entirely unless the theme had a container with a particular id. It now finds the main container of any theme, and falls back to the end of the page.
  • The form no longer needs jQuery on the front end.
  • Fixed: [syrus_contact_form] without an id, which is the form the documentation shows, raised a PHP notice. It now renders nothing, quietly, as it should.
  • Fixed: the consent checkbox had no id and no name, and its label pointed at neither, so selecting the label did not tick the box.
  • Fixed: two forms on the same page gave their fields the same ids. The ids now carry the form’s own.
  • Fixed: in the editor’s preview, changing several fields quickly could leave an older preview on screen.
  • The last Bootstrap class names left anywhere in the plugin are gone. Four of them were spacing utilities in the post editor, where Bootstrap was never loaded at all, so the space they asked for was never there: the social network checkboxes in the Publish box ran into one another.

1.0.0

Everything that follows was built after 0.6.0 and is released here for the first time: a set of tools for running the site, an administration page rebuilt from scratch, and one menu to reach all of it.

New tools, under the Tools menu. None of them involve AI, none of them change anything the plugin already did, and every one is off until you configure it.

  • Code injection in the head, in the footer, before and after the article and in three blocks spread between its paragraphs, with the option to leave any of them out on a single post. The in-article blocks are placed by PHP, so they are there with JavaScript disabled and the text does not shift under the reader.
  • Editorial checks: thirteen rules an article has to satisfy before it can go public, each one a switch of its own. A post that breaks one goes back to Pending, with the problems listed in the Publish box. Administrators can be exempted.
  • Content filters: strip the span tags and the attributes Word and Google Docs leave behind, clean the paragraphs, and rewrite http:// as https://. They act while the page is rendered and never rewrite the post, so switching one off brings the original markup straight back.
  • robots.txt and ads.txt served from the database, each with its own switch. If a real file exists in the root of the install the screen says so, instead of leaving you to wonder why nothing changes.
  • WhatsApp chat: a bubble in the corner of the site that opens the conversation, with an avatar, a greeting and configurable delays. It works with any theme and brings no third-party library with it.
  • Maintenance: close the comments on posts older than a month, delete their revisions, delete the spam and empty the moderation queue. Each task asks for a confirmation, works on a batch of 100 rows and reports how many it touched. Comments awaiting moderation go to the trash rather than being deleted.
  • An upload restriction per user. It filters the upload_files capability, so it also applies to the REST API and to WP-CLI, not only to the buttons on the page. Administrators always keep it, so the screen cannot lock out the person configuring it.
  • Twitter Card meta tags, in the Social Network tab: a link shared on X shows a card crediting the account you name.
  • REST routes under syrus/v1 (theme-version, site-language, site-timezone), for reading remotely what an install is running. They answer anyone; close them with add_filter(‘syrus_ai_rest_public’,’__return_false’).
  • For Yoast users, the page number in front of the description of a paged archive.

All the new screens require administrator permissions, even though the plugin page itself stays open to editors.

The administration page was rebuilt. The same screens, with the same controls and the same behaviour, in the shape WordPress 7.1 gives its own: one rounded panel on a dark field, a header carrying the version, a tab bar, and cards instead of a wall of tables.

  • Bootstrap 5 is gone. It was loaded in full, 228KB of it, to style sixteen admin templates, and its JavaScript was never loaded at all. In its place there is a stylesheet of the plugin’s own, enqueued on the plugin page alone. Animate.css, 71KB that nothing referenced, went with it, and so did the old admin stylesheet. The download is 312KB smaller.
  • Every setting that is on or off is a switch you can see the state of at a glance, instead of a bare checkbox in the second column of a table, and long forms carry a save bar that stays at the bottom of the window.
  • The placeholders for what is not built yet are gone, so the page offers only what it can actually do.

One menu. On a site running the Syrus theme, the plugin builds a single Syrus menu in the sidebar: the theme’s own settings first, then every section of the plugin, each one a direct link. The theme’s entry under Appearance is removed so there is one Syrus menu and not two; deactivating the plugin puts it back. The theme’s screen keeps its own address and its own stylesheet, because the entry is a link to where the theme registered it and not a copy of it. On any other theme nothing changes. The menu is translated, Italian included; it used to be in English whatever the language of the site.

Fixed

  • With the Syrus theme active the plugin page had no link anywhere in wp-admin. It registered its menu under a slug the theme stopped using when it moved its own options screen, and WordPress silently drops a submenu whose parent does not exist, so the page was reachable only by typing the URL.
  • The post editor was getting the plugin’s page background, its gutter and its amber bar, because the plugin’s admin stylesheet was loaded there too. The editor looks like the editor again.
  • On the Social Network tab the Instagram Connect button carried the Twitter button’s id, so the progress spinner appeared on the wrong row, and the Twitter Disconnect button had no id although the script addressed it.
  • Opening the contact form editor without a form, or with an id that no longer exists, raised a PHP warning.

Known: opening the theme’s settings from the Syrus menu highlights Appearance rather than Syrus. WordPress recomputes the current menu for pages registered under a core file and discards what a plugin asks for, so the highlight cannot be moved without taking the page over, which would leave it unstyled.

0.6.0

  • AI Translate means something else now: it translates the posts of this site into another language, from the box in the editor, creating a draft linked to the original. It used to pull articles from external sites through their REST API, along with all the code that involved.
  • Removed the Writesonic rewriting: the AI connector does the same thing.
  • Removed newsmaking. The feature never stored a single row, because the table was missing two of the columns every insert wrote, so there is nothing to preserve: the update drops the empty table and the seven options left behind, the NewsAPI key among them. The cron REST route goes with it.
  • Text and image generation go through the WordPress connectors: the provider keys are managed under Settings > Connectors and the plugin no longer holds any of them.
  • DeepL is registered as a connector, so its key moves to the core screen too.
  • The minimum requirement is now WordPress 7.0, the version the AI Client landed in.
  • The update also drops the translate_and_publish table and the remote domain options, which are no longer needed.

0.5.0

Security, bug fixes and cleanup. No feature removed.

  • Security: closed a chain that let a Subscriber reach every endpoint of the plugin. The bootstrap nonce was printed on any screen you added two parameters to in the URL, the endpoint that mints nonces accepted any action string at all, other plugins’ included, and none of the 41 endpoints checked a capability. Authorization is now centralized, with an endpoint-to-capability map.
  • Security: the contact form handlers verified the nonce but not the capability, and accepted any post id: it was possible to trash any content on the site and hijack the recipient of a form’s email.
  • Security: the cron REST route was public and triggered paid calls, writes and an email. It now requires a shared key.
  • Security: remote domains are validated, where before they allowed requests into the server’s internal network; the OpenAI key is no longer written in clear text into the log table; the API keys are no longer visible to anyone who does not administer the site; certificate verification is restored on the two calls that carry the installation token; HTML arriving from remote sites goes through wp_kses_post().
  • Newsmaking never stored a row: the table was missing two of the columns every insert wrote. The schema is fixed, with a migration for existing installs.
  • Deactivating the plugin no longer deletes the data. Removal happens only on uninstall.
  • Removed session_start() on every request, which stopped any caching system from serving the pages.
  • A failed social share is no longer recorded as a success, and the deprecated library used to send them has been replaced.
  • The filter that discarded form submissions from non-Italian browsers is now a setting, off by default.
  • The Import button on the Import/Export screen never worked, because its script was tied to a tab that does not exist; the same for the button that emptied the newsmaking table and for the Instagram share test.
  • Removed 910 lines of unreachable code and around 600 duplicated ones, 900 KB of unused files, and a var_dump left in production inside a live endpoint.
  • The assets no longer change address on every page load, so the browser can finally cache them.
  • Minimum requirements raised to WordPress 6.5 and PHP 8.1.

0.4.5

  • Maintenance.
